title: Courts and law reform
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:38Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-02T04:41:51Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: None of the bank points explains how court cases expose problems in the law, prompt Parliament to act, or change common law directly; the closest, the courts and NGOs card, covers courts enforcing environmental law rather than law reform.

draft.title: Courts and law reform
card: Courts apply the law to real cases. A case can show that a law is unclear, unfair or out of date.
a judge may point out a problem in a decision. Parliament can then pass a statute to fix it.
common law is law made by judges through their decisions. A court can change it directly by setting a new precedent, if a higher court does not overturn it.
Courts cannot change a statute themselves. Only parliament can amend or repeal a statute, though courts interpret it.
draft.remember: Cases can expose problems that parliament fixes, and courts can change common law themselves.

a.q: A judge finds a statute has a gap that leads to an unfair result, and parliament later amends it. How did the court contribute to reform?
opts: The case exposed the problem and pushed parliament to act
The court amended the statute itself in its judgment
The court changed the common law by creating a precedent
The court wrote the new law and parliament only approved it
a.why: The case revealed the gap, and parliament, which has the power over statutes, made the change. The court did not amend the statute, which is the tempting wrong choice.
a.clue: Who has the power to amend a statute?

b.q: Kai wins a case in the Supreme Court of Victoria, and the judge sets a new rule on a point covered only by common law. What has happened?
opts: The court has changed the common law directly
The court has repealed a statute
Parliament has been forced to pass a new Act
The case has no effect beyond Kai's own dispute
b.why: The point was covered only by common law, which judges make, so the new rule changes it directly. It was not a statute, so repeal is wrong, and parliament was not forced to act.
b.clue: Common law is made by judges, not parliament.

a.best: The case exposed the problem and pushed parliament to act

b.best: The court has changed the common law directly

problems.detail: The distractor 'Parliament has been forced to pass a new Act' uses 'forced', while the card says parliament 'can' act. The absolute word marks the option as wrong without testing the idea.
